h1: The 6 Best Desktop Whiteboards for Notes, Lists and Planning, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 desktop whiteboards, from small magnetic boards on stands to glass panels, scored on size, material, stands and storage.
summary: The Quartet 17 by 23 inch glass desktop panel is the best desktop whiteboard for serious planning, with a ghost-resistant glass surface, magnets and accessory trays. The AMUSIGHT double-sided 16 by 12 inch board is the best compact pick, the Quartet glass pad suits small notes, and the TSJ doubles as a keyboard stand with a drawer.
intro: Ghosting is what ruins a cheap whiteboard. Dry erase ink on a porous surface leaves a faint shadow that no cloth removes, and after a few months a board that was white looks grey and smudged. Glass does not absorb ink, so it erases clean for years, and it is the reason a glass board can cost several times more than a coated one. Whether that premium is worth paying depends on how often you write on it.

We ranked six desktop whiteboards on surface material, writing area, stand design, magnetism and storage. We reviewed listings, which often leave the material of budget boards unstated. A coated board that is double-sided doubles your space, and a glass panel will last longest. Since desk space is limited, we also weigh how much footprint each uses.

products.name: Quartet Glass Whiteboard Desktop Panel, Magnetic, 17"x23", Dry Erase, with Accessory Trays and Magnets (GDP1723W)
products.verdict: A 17 by 23 inch magnetic glass panel with accessory trays and magnets included.
products.description:
The Quartet GDP1723W is a 17 by 23 inch magnetic glass dry erase panel that sits on a desk. It includes accessory trays, magnets and one marker. It costs $100 to $200.

It wins because it has the most writing area and the best surface. Glass resists staining and ghosting, so notes erase cleanly long after cheaper boards have dulled. The magnetic surface holds reminders, and the trays keep markers handy. It is the most expensive and takes real desk depth.

Buy it for tracking several projects at a desk you use daily. Skip it if your desk is small.
products.idealFor: Buyers who need real surface area for tracking multiple ongoing tasks or projects.
products.skipIf: Your desk is tight on space.

products.name: AMUSIGHT Double-Sided Magnetic White Board with Stand, 16" x 12"
products.verdict: Two 16 by 12 inch magnetic writing faces on a stand, under $25.
products.description:
The AMUSIGHT board is 16 by 12 inches with two usable magnetic dry erase faces and a stand. It costs under $25.

Second place goes to it because two faces in one footprint is the best value on a small desk: tasks on one side, a weekly plan on the other. The magnetic surface holds notes. The listing does not state the surface material, so ghosting resistance is unknown.

Buy it for everyday lists in a compact space. Wipe it promptly to limit ghosting.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want two independent writing surfaces in one compact footprint.

products.name: Quartet Dry Erase White Board 9"W x 11"H Desktop Glass Pad with Removable Clip and Marker (GDE119)
products.verdict: A 9 by 11 inch glass pad with a clip and marker, durable and ghost resistant.
products.description:
The Quartet GDE119 is a 9 by 11 inch glass dry erase pad with a removable paper clip and a marker. It costs $25 to $50.

Third place fits because it brings glass to a notepad size. The clip holds a sheet of paper behind the glass, which can show a template or a grid. It is small, so it suits a quick list, not planning.

Buy it for short notes on a crowded desk. For more space, step up to the larger panel.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a durable, ghost-resistant glass surface in a compact size.
products.skipIf: You need room for detailed plans.

products.name: TSJ OFFICE Small Desktop Whiteboard, Glass Dry Erase Board, Computer Keyboard Stand with Drawer
products.verdict: A glass whiteboard that doubles as a keyboard stand, with a built-in drawer.
products.description:
The TSJ OFFICE piece has a glass dry erase surface, a built-in drawer and doubles as a keyboard stand. It costs $25 to $50.

Fourth place suits it because it folds a whiteboard and storage into one desk object, raising the keyboard and holding pens or sticky notes. The listing gives no writing dimensions. Using it as both stand and board means the surface is partly occupied by the keyboard.

Buy it for a tidy small desk. Check the board size.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a whiteboard that also organizes keyboard placement and small supplies.

products.name: White Board with Stand, Small Dry Erase Board, 16"x12" Magnetic Whiteboard
products.verdict: A simple 16 by 12 inch magnetic board with a stand, under $25.
products.description:
This board has a 16 by 12 inch magnetic dry erase surface and a stand. It costs under $25 and the listing does not state the material.

Fifth place fits because it is single-sided, where the next boards offer two faces. It does the job for lists and reminders. Ghosting resistance is unknown.

Buy it for everyday notes. Take a double-sided model if space is tight.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a balanced, general-purpose desktop whiteboard for everyday notes and lists.

products.name: MaxGear Dry Erase Board with Stand, 16"x12" Double-Sided Magnetic Whiteboard, Portable
products.verdict: The lowest-priced double-sided 16 by 12 inch magnetic board with a stand.
products.description:
The MaxGear board is a 16 by 12 inch double-sided magnetic dry erase board with a stand, and the cheapest of the roundup at under $25.

It ranks last because it matches the AMUSIGHT for less and says less. Double-sided and portable, it works for lists and plans. Material is unstated.

Buy it if price is the deciding factor. The AMUSIGHT is better documented.
products.idealFor: Budget-conscious buyers who want a functional double-sided board without extra features.

whatMatters.detail: Glass does not absorb ink and erases cleanly for years. Coated boards are cheaper but can ghost. Choose glass if you write daily.
A 9 by 11 inch pad suits quick notes, 16 by 12 suits lists, and 17 by 23 suits planning. Match size to the job and your desk.
Two faces double the space in one footprint. Flip to a clean side while the first is in use. Check that both are writable.
A magnetic surface holds notes and pins without marking it. Included magnets are a bonus. Look for magnetic in the listing.
A stand should hold the board upright against marker pressure. Wobble is a common complaint. Check for a stand and its description.

faq.a: Wipe the board soon after writing, use fresh markers, and clean with a whiteboard cleaner now and then. Glass resists ghosting better than coated boards.
Using permanent markers or leaving ink for weeks. Use dry erase markers and erase regularly.
For daily use, yes, since they stay clean. For occasional notes a cheap board is fine.

faq.q: How do I set up the stand?
faq.a: Slot the board into the stand or unfold the legs, and place it on a flat surface. Check it does not rock.

faq.q: Will magnets stick to all of them?
faq.a: Those listed as magnetic will. Check the listing, as non-magnetic boards will not hold magnets.
Wipe with a dry cloth, then use whiteboard cleaner or a damp cloth. Glass can take glass cleaner.

finalTake: The Quartet 17 by 23 inch glass panel is the best desktop whiteboard for planning, with a clean surface and room to work. The AMUSIGHT is the best compact board, the small Quartet pad suits quick notes, and the TSJ adds storage and a keyboard stand.
